title: Dark matter mass fraction in axion stars
abstract: QCD axion dark matter is fragmented into small mass miniclusters of high density. With the natural parameters of miniclusters, the time for Bose-Einstein condensation is less than the age of the Universe, which leads to the formation of Bose stars inside these structures. Recently, the problem of the subsequent growth of Bose stars was solved analytically (Dmitriev et al, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 091001 (2024)). We use this solution to determine present day mass fraction of dark matter in Bose stars and their mass function.

title: Revisiting Evidence of Temperature Fluctuations in H II Regions. I. Interionic temperature differences
abstract: The oxygen abundance of H II regions is a fundamental tracer of chemical enrichment and gas cycling and is now routinely measured across a broad range of cosmic time. A persistent complication is the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF): the O$^{++}$/H$^+$ abundance inferred from optical recombination lines (RLs) is systematically higher than that inferred from collisionally excited lines (CELs). Small-scale temperature fluctuations within the O$^{++}$-emitting gas are among the most widely discussed explanations for this discrepancy. However, the recent identification of a substantial continuum-pumping contribution to the O II spectrum of M42 motivates a renewed assessment of which observations uniquely favor a temperature-based interpretation and which are also compatible with other mechanisms. In this first paper of a series, I examine the relation between the inferred temperature-fluctuation parameter, $t^2$, and interionic temperature differences, focusing on $ΔT_e=T_e([OIII])-T_e([NII])$. Photoionization calculations show that ionization stratification naturally produces systematic temperature differences between the low- and high-ionization zones. Meanwhile, the conversion from an ADF to $t^2$ is strongly temperature dependent because CEL emissivities are nonlinear functions of electron temperature. I show that these two effects can account for much of the observed $t^2$-$ΔT_e$ relation without requiring the interionic temperature difference itself to trace fluctuations within the O$^{++}$ zone. This result does not exclude temperature fluctuations in H II regions. Instead, it indicates that interionic temperature differences should be interpreted with care and, on their own, provide limited discrimination among proposed origins of the ADF.

title: Continuum Pumping Revises Metallicity in the Orion Nebula
abstract: The enrichment of heavy elements in the interstellar medium is central to understanding galaxy evolution. Oxygen, the most abundant element after H and He, provides the principal tracer of gas-phase metallicity, typically measured using nebular emission lines in star-forming regions. However, a long-standing issue-the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF)-produces a $\sim 0.25$ dex offset between metallicities derived from recombination lines (RLs) and collisionally excited lines (CELs). We present deep spectroscopic observations of the Orion Nebula (M42), and use them to assess the contribution of the often neglected continuum pumping process. We find that the continuum pumping effect is at least a factor of two stronger than previously expected. After accounting for the flux contribution from continuum pumping, the RL metallicity is consistent with the CEL metallicity, thus explaining the bulk of the ADF. Reassessing O/H measurements in five literature star-forming regions using the same method, we similarly find a systematic reduction of RL-based metallicities. These results indicate that RL metallicities, which have previously been considered more reliable than CELs, are subject to potentially large bias from continuum pumping. This study provides a foundation to correct this bias and establish accurate element abundance scales throughout cosmic time.

title: Environmental dependence of the properties of H$α$ emitters in the extremely massive galaxy protoclusters BOSS1244 and BOSS1542 at $z = 2.24$
abstract: Protoclusters, the progenitors of galaxy clusters, provide ideal laboratories for studying how high-density environments influence galaxy formation and evolution at early cosmic epochs. It remains unclear whether environmental effects on galaxy properties over scales of $>30$ cMpc are already in place at $z > 2$ and how these effects depend on the evolutionary stage of large-scale structures. We investigate the physical properties of H$α$ emitters (HAEs) in two extremely overdense protoclusters, BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, at $z = 2.24$, and explore the environmental dependence of galaxy properties at this redshift. In BOSS1244, we find a clear color-density and stellar mass-density relation. HAEs in higher-density regions are significantly redder in $z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}$ and more massive than those in lower-density regions. In contrast, BOSS1542 shows weak or no such correlations. Red HAEs $(z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}>2.5)$ in both fields are preferentially located in the densest cores, have high stellar masses $(>10^{11}\,M_{\odot})$, high SFRs, and are $4-7$ times more abundant than in general fields. The irregular morphologies observed in some red HAEs are consistent with ongoing mass assembly and may be associated with dust-obscured star formation or galaxy interactions. Both protoclusters broadly follow the star-forming main sequence, but BOSS1542 exhibits a steeper slope, indicating more active star formation in massive galaxies. Our results demonstrate that environmental effects on galaxy properties operate over scales of $\sim39$\,cMpc at $z=2.24$, but their manifestation is strongly dependent on the evolutionary state of the large-scale structure. BOSS1244 appears more evolved, with ongoing galaxy merging and possible quenching, while BOSS1542 remains in an early, filamentary, gas-rich phase.

title: XRISM view of a featureless cluster Abell 1060: Revealing the advection of a diffuse radio source by ICM motions
abstract: Abell 1060 is a nearby, dynamically relaxed galaxy cluster hosting the extended radio structure Flying Fox (FF) near its center. We used high-resolution XRISM/Resolve spectroscopy to measure intracluster medium (ICM) motions and velocity dispersion. Spatially resolved analysis reveals a velocity gradient of approximately 100 km/s along FF and enhanced velocity dispersion near the brightest cluster galaxy NGC 3311, suggesting turbulence generated by galaxy-ICM interactions. These results and the compact extent of FF favor fossil plasma supplied by past activity of the brightest cluster galaxy and transported by ICM motions. We also tested whether the measured turbulence could generate or maintain the nonthermal components of FF. For a velocity dispersion of $96.7^{+23.9}_{-24.6}$ km/s and an assumed turbulence scale of 50 kpc, comparable to the Resolve field of view and approximately half the cluster core radius, the turbulent energy flux is approximately $3.49 \times 10^{-28}$ erg cm$^{-3}$ s$^{-1}$. Although this flux may weakly reenergize pre-existing relativistic electrons, the acceleration timescale of approximately 2.5 Gyr exceeds the synchrotron and inverse Compton cooling timescale of approximately 210 Myr. The present turbulence is therefore insufficient to accelerate electrons to high energies. In situ turbulent reacceleration is unlikely to dominate the generation of FF, although it may help maintain fossil electrons supplied by past AGN activity. These results link ICM dynamics to the origin of nonthermal emission and support a time-evolutionary picture of particle acceleration in galaxy clusters.

title: A Tributary of Tucana III? The Sutlej Stellar Stream in DELVE DR3
abstract: We present the first analysis of the Sutlej stellar stream using deep DECam photometry from the third data release of the DECam Local Volume Exploration Survey (DELVE DR3). Sutlej was discovered in Gaia DR3 as two parallel branches of old, metal-poor stars in projection near the SMC. Our DELVE DR3 sample reaches $\sim$2.5-3.5 mag below the main-sequence turnoff of Sutlej, and with a main-sequence matched filter built from an isochrone fit to Sutlej, we recover both previously identified branches, and find additional structure between them and at the periphery of the stream, occupying a region of $\sim$11$^\circ$ $\times$ 7$^\circ$ scattered at $\sim$23-33 kpc. We investigate this region by separating it into four segments that have Sutlej-like properties. The isochrone is also consistent with the nearby ultra-faint satellite Tucana III (Tuc III), and the two systems have similar distances and proper motions. $N$-body simulations of a Tuc III-like satellite show that, once the passage of a massive LMC is accounted for, Tuc III's preceding pericentric passage was deep enough to strip most of the progenitor. The encounter with the LMC then spreads the debris across the Sutlej field at the observed distances and proper motions, though the models do not recreate the observed discrete overdensities. We find that Sutlej is compatible with a Tuc III origin.

title: py4radiation: a framework for generating heating/cooling functions and ion fractions from custom radiation fields for astrophysical simulations
abstract: Modelling multiphase gas in and around galaxies is key to understanding the baryon cycle in galaxy evolution. Modern simulation codes rely on heating/cooling functions and ion fractions to capture the thermodynamics and chemistry of such gases, but coupling all physical factors remains challenging. We present a new Python-based, parallelised package that acts as an integration framework, connecting well-established astrophysical codes and models to produce self-consistent heating/cooling functions and ion fractions from custom ionising UV/X-ray backgrounds. The package returns multi-dimensional tables that can be readily coupled to hydrodynamic and post-processing codes to study radiative processes and extract observables, as we demonstrate with static cloud simulations. Our simulation suite studies the thermodynamic history of a static circumgalactic cloud with smoothed edges subjected to meta-galactic and starburst heating. We find that the clouds experience damped pulsations regulated by strong cooling-driven inflows and heating-driven outflows that constantly overshoot pressure equilibrium. Meta-galactic heating is weak and produces a confined and dense cloud, while starburst heating is strong and sustains large clouds only a little smaller than those obtained with the standard $10^4\,\rm K$ cooling floor. Starburst radiative heating acts as a damping agent, thereby reducing mixing. py4radiation comes with extensive documentation and a sample catalogue of heating/cooling functions and ion tables for a selected set of input meta-galactic and starburst spectral energy distributions. The code is publicly available and can be easily expanded.

title: Multiphase Gas in the Ram-Pressure-Stripped Elliptical Galaxy NGC 1404
abstract: Galaxy groups and low-mass galaxy clusters are major sites of environment-driven galaxy evolution. NGC 1404 is an X-ray-bright early-type galaxy traveling through the intracluster medium of the nearby low-mass Fornax Cluster, and it hosts off-center warm ionized gas. With minimal ongoing stellar feedback and negligible active galactic nucleus feedback, NGC 1404 provides an ideal laboratory for constraining the impact of environmental processes on the thermodynamics of the interstellar medium. We analyzed VLT/MUSE, 506 ks Chandra ACIS, and 119 ks XMM-Newton RGS observations to quantify gas motions in both the hot and warm phases of NGC 1404. We probed the kinematics of the warm gas by deriving the velocity structure function (VSF) from MUSE H$α$ integral-field spectroscopy. To measure the kinematics of the hot gas, we derived the power spectrum of X-ray surface brightness fluctuations from the Chandra data, and independently constrained galaxy-scale hot gas motions by measuring Fe XVII resonant scattering and turbulent line broadening with RGS. Our RGS spectral analysis gives a three-dimensional Mach number of $0.48^{+0.22}_{-0.14}$, consistent with the power-spectrum results from Chandra for the same extraction region, and corresponding to a turbulent-to-thermal energy density ratio of $\sim0.13$. The warm-gas VSF follows the expectation for Kolmogorov turbulence and is broadly consistent with the hot-gas kinematics. The off-center warm gas in NGC 1404 may have formed through radiative cooling of the hot interstellar medium, triggered by the uplift of low-entropy hot gas during ram pressure stripping. Our study suggests that ram pressure stripping can drive substantial gas motions and reshape the thermodynamic state of the interstellar medium of cluster member galaxies.

title: Unresolved binaries from Gaia XP to SPHEREx
abstract: Unresolved companions alter the luminosity and spectra of a star, but a colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) reveals them only when the system is over-luminous, and a Gaia photocentre orbit constrains only a combination of the mass and flux ratios. We fit the absolute Gaia BP/RP (XP) and SPHEREx spectra (XPS) of about 71,000 low-mass stars in the Gaia Catalogue of Nearby Stars with the J-CaPS XPS emulator, which predicts single-star and coeval-binary spectra on an absolute flux scale. First, more than half of known binaries lie within the main-sequence (MS) band of the CMD, because the companion is faint or lifts a metal-poor primary onto the single-star ridge. XPS recovers 86 per cent of the binaries that a CMD cut finds and 44 per cent of those it misses. Second, a small photocentre motion can come from a faint companion or a luminous one of nearly equal mass. XPS distinguishes them and recovers the mass ratios of double-lined binaries. Among substellar candidates with radial-velocity follow-up, it ranks all 11 binaries above all 16 confirmed brown-dwarf or planet hosts. The public package spbin provides this check before follow-up. Third, where XPS detects no companion light, we place an upper limit on the light of an MS companion. Among Gaia DR3 astrometric orbits with clean spectral fits, 2841 require more companion mass than XPS allows for a single MS star. Within 200 pc, their companion masses cluster at those of typical white dwarfs, and nearly circular orbits support this interpretation. Of 24 companions that joint radial-velocity and astrometric orbits show to be faint, XPS recovers 22, compared with 14 selected by the absence of a colour excess. Applied to forthcoming Gaia DR4 orbital solutions, XPS can help distinguish luminous binaries from substellar companions and identify candidate compact companions whose dynamical masses exceed the limits allowed by their light.

title: Velocity-Window Dependence of the Broad H$α$ Width-Luminosity Relation in Little Red Dots
abstract: Broad Balmer emission lines probe black hole masses and nuclear kinematics in high-redshift active galactic nuclei (AGNs). In JWST "little red dots" (LRDs), integrated broad-H$α$ widths span a remarkably narrow range at fixed line luminosity, raising the question of whether this tightness persists once outer-wing emission is included. Holding each object and its broad-H$α$ luminosity fixed, we measure the finite-window line dispersion $σ(V)$, the flux-weighted second-moment width within $\pm V$, from $V = 1500$ to $4500~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in JWST/NIRSpec spectra and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) Type-1 AGNs. Across 20 high signal-to-noise LRDs, the observed scatter in $\log_{10}σ(V)$ at fixed $L_{\mathrm{H}α}$ rises from 0.036 to 0.084 dex between $V = 2500$ and $4500~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, a paired increase of 0.048 dex with a 95% bootstrap interval of 0.026-0.064 dex, compared with 0.020 dex across 167 broader SDSS AGNs. Injecting synthetic profiles into the empirical noise of the same 20 spectra shows that single-Gaussian and core-plus-wing models both accommodate this rise, leaving intrinsic wing diversity, truncation, and wing noise unseparated. In the clearest dual-line spectrum, RUBIES-EGS-55604, H$β$ strengthens relative to H$α$ from line center to wing under two spectral decompositions of the same grating spectrum. Alongside integrated widths in JWST, SDSS, and 334 Euclid DR1 AGNs, these results show that the observed tightness of the H$α$ scaling depends on the velocities included in $σ(V)$, requiring mass and kinematic models to match both transition and velocity interval.

title: Discovery of Two Hyperluminous Infrared Galaxies at $z\sim6$
abstract: Hyperluminous infrared galaxies (HyLIRGs) at cosmic dawn are key to understanding the formation of the first massive galaxies. We report the spectroscopic confirmation of two unlensed HyLIRGs at $z\sim6$ in the COSMOS field, AzTECC63 and S2COS-84, originally selected from single-dish AzTEC and SCUBA-2 surveys. Using ALMA and NOEMA observations, we robustly detected CO and [CII] lines in both galaxies and unambiguously confirmed their redshifts to be $z=6.092$ and $z=5.90$, respectively. Panchromatic SED fitting reveals dust-obscured star formation rates of $\approx1000$ and $\approx2300\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, ranking them among the most intensely star-forming systems known at $z \gtrsim 6$. High-resolution ALMA observations reveal an extremely compact morphology for S2COS-84, with a dust-continuum effective radius of $\approx0.3$ kpc, implying a star-formation rate surface density above the Eddington limit. The far-infrared SEDs of both galaxies, together with the compact size of S2COS-84, indicate warm dust ($T_{\rm dust} \approx 80$ K) that is likely optically thick at far-infrared wavelengths. Both galaxies exhibit an extreme [CII] deficit, with $L_{\rm [C\,II]}/L_{\rm IR} \approx 10^{-3.7}$, an order of magnitude below that of normal star-forming galaxies. Their molecular gas masses, derived consistently from both [C\,{\sc ii}] and dust, together with their IR-derived SFRs imply short gas depletion times of $\approx$40--60 Myr, making them plausible progenitors of the earliest massive quiescent galaxies found at $z\sim5$.

title: Modeling the chemical impacts of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes
abstract: Some protostars undergo episodic accretion, resulting in luminosity outbursts that heat their envelopes. The increase in temperature alters the position of the snowlines, which return to their original locations on different timescales depending on the species. However, the chemical effects of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes, including their long-term consequences, remain poorly explored. We investigate the chemical impact of luminosity outbursts on the envelope of a solar-type protostar, accounting for its dynamics, and identify trends in the molecular response relative to both ongoing and past outburst activity. We combined the dynamic semi-analytic code APE with the three-phase chemical model NAUTILUS to predict the time evolution of 83 molecular abundances between 10 and 10,000 au in the collapsing envelope. The outburst was parameterized by increasing the protostellar luminosity by a factor of 100 for 100 years. The outburst shifts molecular snowlines outward by up to a factor of ten, thus enriching the gas phase through thermal desorption. Most species return to their pre-outburst state within a few thousand years at most for r$\leq$1000 au and remain in that state thereafter. However, eight molecules (HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, C2H5CHO, OCS, SO2, C2S, C3S, and HC3N) show abundance deviations 10$-$50 kyr after the outburst in the warm inner regions (T$\geq$100 K), due to the inward transport of chemically altered material. Eight other species (CH3O, C2O, NH2, HCCO, HCNO, HNO, NO, and NCO) show enhanced gas-phase abundances at intermediate radii ($\sim$300$-$1500 au). Overall, most molecules are impacted by outward snowline shifts. With the exception of HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, and C2H5CHO, all complex organic molecules (COMs) are expected to exhibit similar abundances in the warm inner regions of protostars (hot corino), regardless of whether they undergo outbursts.

title: Integrated Study of NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437 Open Clusters: from Stellar Parameters to Orbital Trajectories Utilizing Gaia DR3 Archive
abstract: We present a comprehensive photometric, astrometric, and dynamical study of four Galactic open clusters, NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437, using Gaia DR3 data. Probable cluster members were identified through astrometric and photometric criteria. Radial density profiles were modelled with a King-type surface-density distribution to derive structural parameters. Mean parallaxes and proper motions yielded astrometric distances of 410 +/- 12 pc (NGC 1662), 1761 +/- 335 pc (NGC 1778), 477 +/- 18 pc (NGC 2422), and 1681 +/- 172 pc (NGC 2437). Fundamental astrophysical parameters were estimated through Bayesian isochrone fitting using PARSEC evolutionary models within an MCMC framework. The resulting ages (log(t/yr)) are 8.91 (-0.33/+0.24), 8.20 (-0.11/+0.18), 7.80 (-0.11/+0.06), and 8.56 (-0.34/+0.27), respectively. Luminosity functions were transformed into present-day mass functions using an isochrone-based mass-luminosity relation. The derived mass-function slopes are broadly consistent, within uncertainties, with the classical Salpeter form. Mean systemic radial velocities from Gaia DR3 and complementary spectroscopic surveys enabled the determination of Galactic space velocities (U, V, W) in the Local Standard of Rest frame. Backward orbital integrations over 3 Gyr were performed using galpy with the MWPotential2014 Galactic potential. The resulting orbits are nearly circular (e <= 0.106), with limited vertical excursions (Z_max < 0.3 kpc), consistent with thin-disc kinematics. Inferred birth radii suggest possible outward radial displacement for NGC 2422, NGC 2437, and NGC 1778, and inward displacement for NGC 1662. Overall, all four clusters appear to have evolved within relatively stable Galactic disc orbits.

title: Outflows and Young Stars in the Auriga-California Giant Molecular Cloud
abstract: The Auriga-California Molecular Cloud (AMC) is a nearby star-forming region with a moderate level of star formation activity. Previous infrared surveys have shown that its young stellar population is concentrated along a dense filament extending north of NGC 1579. We searched for new manifestations of ongoing star formation in the AMC by identifying optical and molecular outflows, Hα emission-line stars, and young stars associated with reflection nebulae. Narrowband Hα and [SII] imaging, together with slitless spectroscopy, were obtained with the 1-m Schmidt telescope of the Byurakan Observatory. The optical data were complemented by near-infrared images from the Spitzer Enhanced Imaging Products (SEIP) and by WISE/unWISE archival data. We discovered seven new Herbig-Haro (HH) objects and outflows associated with several young stellar objects, including deeply embedded infrared sources and stars surrounded by compact reflection nebulae. Nearly all of the optical HH objects have molecular hydrogen counterparts, and several additional candidate H2 outflows without optical counterparts were identified. Particularly noteworthy is a compact region around V347 Per that appears to host at least three molecular outflows. We also present a list of newly identified Hα emission-line stars and a catalogue of stars associated with optical reflection nebulae. Both populations are concentrated primarily along the northern dark filament of the cloud. The spatial distribution of the newly identified HH objects, molecular outflows, emission-line stars, and nebulous young stars confirms that the northern filament is the principal site of ongoing star formation in the AMC. The close correspondence between the optical and molecular outflowsfurther suggests that most of their driving sources are deeply embedded Class 0/I young stellar objects.

title: Constraining Dehnen-inspired dark matter halo with S2 star's orbit
abstract: We use the orbit of S2 star around Sagittarius A* to constrain three black hole backgrounds motivated by Dehnen profiles with inner slopes $γ=0$, $1$, and $5/2$, which are characterized by the scale radius $r_s$ and density $ρ_s$ of the dark matter halo. An exact turning-point integral gives the pericenter advance at finite eccentricity, and an exterior expansion identifies the leading halo contributions. A fifteen-parameter Bayesian analysis combines astrometric and spectroscopic observations with the measured precession parameter, from which we obtain the marginalized $1σ$ upper limits $r_s/M<0.236$, $0.168$, and $0.030$, and $ρ_sM^2<0.536$, $0.578$, and $0.004$, respectively. The leading halo monopole in the first two metrics is degenerate with the central mass. At fixed dynamical mass, their leading radial profile correction produces retrograde precession. The $γ=5/2$ metric introduces an additional angular deficit contribution, which enhances the precession response and accounts for its smaller parameter limits.

title: Identifying Distant and Highly Reddened Star Clusters: 486 Open Clusters and Candidates in the Dusty Galactic Disk
abstract: The Gaia mission has transformed the census of Galactic star clusters. Most discoveries were based on Gaia DR2 and EDR3, and the rate of new large cluster catalogues has declined since 2023. The distant and dusty part of the disk is still poorly sampled because optical data are strongly affected by extinction. We search for star clusters in the Galactic disk using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, together with 2MASS near-infrared photometry. We scan trial cluster centers in Galactic position, proper motion, and parallax space, assign a Bayesian membership probability to each star, construct a relative density map, and use DBSCAN solely to separate neighboring peaks. We identify 486 clusters and candidates with astrometric quality comparable to that of previously reported clusters. Of these, 450 have no literature counterpart, while 36 are known clusters that were not recovered in earlier Gaia cluster searches. The median distance is 6.9 kpc, and 39% of the objects lie beyond 8 kpc. The median extinction is Av = 5.10 mag, and 16% of the objects have Av > 8mag. The new objects fill a sparsely sampled region of the distance--extinction plane. Their distribution reveals the north--south displacement of the Galactic warp, and high-latitude objects are on average farther, older, and less extincted. Gaia DR3 still offers room for distant, dust-obscured clusters, and this sample provides a baseline for Gaia DR4. All cluster parameters, member star information, spatial distribution maps, and color-magnitude diagrams can be downloaded from https://zenodo.org/records/24431850.

title: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
abstract: We validate a subset of the astrometric accelerations reported in Gaia DR3 non-single-star solutions by their consistency with the gravitational pull of known, resolved companions. Cross-matching 338,215 DR3 acceleration solutions against the Washington Double Star (WDS) catalog of visual binaries yields 2,466 unique pairs within 2". For each pair we compare the measured acceleration with alpha_max, the Newtonian bound on the acceleration the companion can impart on the Gaia-tracked photocenter. For 98.1% of the pairs the measured acceleration exceeds this bound by more than a factor of 10, so the cataloged companion cannot be responsible and the perturber must be a closer, unresolved one. The remaining 45 plausible wide binaries are close pairs at the WDS resolution limit. We fit orbits with an updated orvara, extended to accept the DR3 acceleration and jerk coefficients as direct constraints and released with htof as part of this work. The fits converge for 16 of the 45 and one boundary case, the rest having too few resolved measures or a perturber other than the cataloged pair, and 13 of the 17 carry enough data to test the coefficients. Eleven of the 13 statistically accommodate the reported accelerations, for seven- and nine-parameter solutions alike, and the dynamical companion masses agree with the photometric estimates where the photocenter conversion is well determined. Independently of the fits, 33 of the 43 plausible systems with a usable position angle (77%) have the acceleration directed within 45 degrees of the primary-companion axis, against 50% for a control sample: DR3's measured accelerations point in the directions of the cataloged companions.

title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
abstract: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $γ= 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $δΦ_2 \propto a_b^2$. We also examine the donor's response to periodic forcing from the inner binary and find a transition between individual and collaborative accretion that determines whether the transferred material can form and sustain a circumbinary disk. Our results show that the finite separation of the inner binary can strongly regulate both the rate and fate of tertiary mass transfer, constraining a poorly understood phase of hierarchical triple evolution.

title: Chemical structure of the solar neighbourhood with DESI DR1
abstract: We analyse the chemical, spatial, and kinematic properties of stars in the solar neighbourhood using DESI Data Release 1 combined with Gaia astrometry. A high-quality FGK dwarf sample is separated into low-$α$ and high-$α$ populations using Gaussian mixture modelling in the [$α$/Fe]--[Fe/H] plane. The low-$α$ population is more metal rich, dominates near the Galactic mid-plane, and shows negative radial and vertical metallicity gradients. The high-$α$ population is more metal poor, has a steeper vertical metallicity gradient, an approximately flat radial metallicity profile, and dynamically hotter kinematics. Despite these differences, the two chemically defined populations overlap substantially in velocity space. These results indicate distinct chemical enrichment histories for the low-$α$ and high-$α$ populations, while showing that chemical classification does not map uniquely onto present-day kinematic components. The observed chemo-dynamical structure is consistent with the combined effects of chemical enrichment, radial redistribution, and secular dynamical evolution in shaping the Galactic disc.

title: Age dependence of the radial metallicity gradient in the Galactic disc with LAMOST and Gaia
abstract: We investigate the stellar radial metallicity ([Fe/H]) gradient--age relation (MGAR) of the Galactic disc using a solar-neighbourhood sample of 580\,037 F-, G-, and K-type (FGK) dwarf and turn-off stars from LAMOST DR7, Gaia Data Release3, and the corrected StarHorse age catalogue. The fiducial MGAR is non-monotonic, with relatively strong negative gradients at intermediate ages followed by substantial flattening towards older populations. The most negative gradient occurs at $6$--$8$ Gyr in the adopted 2-Gyr bins, although the $4$--$6$ Gyr slope is statistically similar, indicating a broad intermediate-age turnover rather than a sharply defined transition. The flattening persists within the low-$α$ population, indicating that chemical-population mixing alone cannot explain the full-sample relation, and is also recovered under alternative guiding-radius definitions, radial fitting ranges, vertical-orbit selections, propagation of the reported random age uncertainties, and an alternative stellar-age scale. In contrast, controlling the age-dependent $T_{\rm eff}$--$\log g$ distribution substantially reduces the absolute gradient amplitudes and modifies the younger-age behaviour. A same-star comparison with APOGEE DR17 further shows that the broad age dependence of the controlled MGAR is recovered using an external [Fe/H] scale. We therefore identify the intermediate-to-old-age flattening as the most robust feature of the observed MGAR, whereas the precise location and depth of the intermediate-age minimum and the detailed younger-age morphology are less stable. These results indicate that stellar-parameter selection can contribute to the diversity of MGAR morphologies reported in previous studies.

title: The JWST Resolved Stellar Populations Early Release Science Program. X. Cross-Observatory Proper Motion Measurements with HST and JWST
abstract: We present the first absolute systemic proper motion (PM) of a galaxy measured by combining Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and JWST imaging. The PM of WLM, an isolated dwarf galaxy at $\sim$1 Mpc, is measured against background galaxies with Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) F814W imaging from 2015 and 2024 and NIRCam imaging from 2022 and 2024. The two ACS epochs give a systemic PM of $(μ_α^*, μ_δ) = (+0.087 \pm 0.019, -0.079 \pm 0.017)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 145 galaxies over 8.93 years, which agrees with previous Gaia-based PMs to within 0.4$σ$ and is the most precise PM of WLM. For the HST-to-JWST PMs, we fit each NIRCam detector separately, match the point-spread functions with empirically derived convolution kernels, and correct biases with injected galaxies. With an F090W second epoch, the PM is $(+0.081 \pm 0.045, -0.113 \pm 0.046)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 43 galaxies over 7.02 years, which, like the F150W PM, agrees with HST-to-HST over the same area to within 1$σ$, while F200W differs by $\sim$2$σ$. The long-wavelength F250M and F430M PMs are consistent to within 1$σ$, though less precise. Fewer galaxies can be used at wavelengths farther from F814W. A cross-observatory systematic of $\sim$0.05 mas yr$^{-1}$ cannot be ruled out over 7 years. At equal baselines, an F090W second epoch is at least as precise as our second ACS epoch over the same area. We recommend the NIRCam filter closest in wavelength to the first-epoch filter, though the long-wavelength filters show promise for closer targets or longer baselines.

title: Modeling extraordinary relativistic jets on the scale of the cosmic web
abstract: Recent observations of supermassive black hole jets extending up to the typical sizes of cosmic web filaments challenge our current understanding. In particular, the overall jet size of J152932.16+601534.4 ("Porphyrion") reaches $\sim 7$ Mpc at redshift 0.896. Magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) models of relativistic jets have never been successfully applied to such extraordinary distances, requiring demanding jet-environment and flow stability conditions. By using state-of-the-art numerical simulations of 3D relativistic-MHD jets, we show that Porphyrion's observational properties can be successfully modelled in a realistic scenario, involving a jet kinetic power of $3.5 \times 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and an external medium of a low-density galaxy group. We find that the pair of jets expands to $\sim 9$ Mpc in about $20$ Myr, implying that the jet grows with relativistic speeds for most of its evolution. Comparing this case with other jets of similar power propagating in substantially denser cosmic structures, we find much slower outflows that can only reach a few Mpc, consistent with the bulk of the observed population of giant radio galaxies. Our results make a testable prediction, i.e. future detections of even larger-scale jets in upcoming surveys and database searches will be invaluable in studying the demographics and feedback of the poorly known population of powerful jets, particularly in under-dense regions of the cosmic web.

title: The FRB Population Revisited: Rate, Energy, Evolution, and Host-DM Constraints from the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
abstract: We present a study that simultaneously fits for key fast radio burst (FRB) population properties using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog while calibrating for instrumental selection effects. Our inferred volumetric rate at $z=0$ is $1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3}\times 10^{5}\,{\rm Gpc}^{-3}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ above an isotropic-equivalent energy of $10^{39}$ erg and below a scattering timescale of 30 ms at 600 MHz. The evolution of the FRB rate relative to the cosmic star formation rate remains statistically unconstrained. Assuming a Schechter function for the energy distribution, isotropic emission, and 1-GHz emission bandwidth, we find a characteristic maximum energy of $2.0^{+2.6}_{-1.0} \times 10^{41}$ erg and a differential power-law index of $-1.41\,^{+0.27}_{-0.21}({\rm stat.})\,\pm\,0.35({\rm sys.})$. The host galaxy contribution to the observed dispersion measure (DM) is modeled as a log-normal distribution; assuming a total Galactic contribution of 80 $\text{pc cm}^{-3}$, we find a median host-galaxy DM contribution of $199^{+34}_{-36}\;\text{pc cm}^{-3}$ in the rest-frame. Finally, we find that the average FRB spectrum, described by a spectral index of $α=-1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$, is inconsistent with being flat at the $\sim2σ$ level. We note an excess of high-S/N bursts at low DMs in the observed sample that is not predicted by the best-fit model. Testing alternative models does not alleviate this tension; future population studies may mitigate this limitation by incorporating robust fluence and redshift measurements.

title: Kinetic moment estimates and a one-sided Lyapunov barrier for the relativistic fermionic Michie-King equation
abstract: We study the cutoff Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR), or relativistic fermionic Michie--King, equation of state along an equilibrium family with fixed Tolman--Klein invariants. Three kinetic moments give exact formulas for both the pressure-to-density ratio and the derivative of pressure. Cauchy--Schwarz yields a global relation between these two quantities. It implies vertical vector-field domination of the associated Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff system by the linear equation of state $P=ρc^2/\sqrt3$ in the physical wedge $0<y\leq3x$. We construct a filled, one-sided version of the Bors--Stańczy Lyapunov barrier and check every boundary. This controls all outward excursions, including those after a lower exit from a Lyapunov sublevel. For regular configurations the resulting explicit Lambert bound is $2Gm(r)/(rc^2)<0.6879212521$. Using the diagonal where this ratio has a stationary value sharpens the bound to $0.6734385929$. The argument is conditional on a regular TOV configuration and does not require a separate finite-radius existence theorem. We also identify and correct a logarithmic coefficient in the previously used explicit linear-comparator formula.

title: Resolved internal dynamics of a globular cluster candidate in a cosmological simulation at cosmic dawn
abstract: Globular clusters (GCs) are among the oldest and densest stellar systems in the Universe. Their compact sizes and old ages imply they must have assembled rapidly in the early Universe, yet the detailed physical mechanisms responsible for their formation remain uncertain. Although several scenarios have been proposed, cosmological simulations have so far been unable to resolve their detailed formation and internal dynamical structure at birth. Using a cosmological simulation that uniquely combines sub-parsec resolution with the formation of individual star particles, we follow the gravitational collapse and assembly of a compact stellar system with GC-progenitor mass and size, while directly resolving its internal dynamics and tracing the build-up of its angular momentum. The system assembles most of its stellar mass within 3 Myr, at $z\simeq10.5$, it rapidly becomes gas-poor, star-dominated, and develops ordered internal rotation acquired largely through the hierarchical assembly of distinct stellar subsystems. It forms as a satellite of a larger stellar complex within the virial radius of the $M_{\rm vir}\simeq1.73\times10^8\,M_\odot$ dark-matter halo hosting it. Its density, size and mass overlap with those of compact stellar systems recently observed by JWST at high redshift. These results indicate that GC progenitors can have well-defined internal kinematic structures already after their formation.

title: Quasi-hostless LRDs with intrinsically red, faint UV continua
abstract: High-redshift objects characterised by very weak UV relative to their strong, red rest-optical continua, with broad Balmer lines, appear to represent little red dots (LRDs) in their purest form: sources dominated by emission from their central engine (CE), sometimes dubbed black hole stars (BH*s). Previous work has selected BH*-dominated objects, where a BH* template dominates the rest-optical emission; this remains agnostic to the rest-UV. We therefore select low FUV-to-optical continuum ratio ($L_{\rm 1500}/L_{5100}<0.03$) objects resembling MoM-BH* and The Cliff, from a spectroscopic sample of 132 LRDs at $2\lesssim z\lesssim9$. This identifies three LRDs that we newly classify as BH*-like objects, more than doubling the existing sample: two at $z>6$ and one at $z\sim3$. The UV slope reddens as the NUV- ($L_{\rm 3500}$) and FUV-to-optical ratios fall, with $β_{\rm UV}$ rising from $-1.8$ at $L_{\rm 1500}/L_{5100}\sim 0.5$ to $-0.5$ at $L_{\rm 1500}/L_{5100}<0.03$, beyond values typically seen at these redshifts. As the UV-to-optical ratio weakens, gas-enshrouded BH emission appears to dominate, leading to the quasi-hostless regime: a weak, red UV continuum emerges alongside extreme Balmer decrements and weak forbidden line emission. This reddening could be reproduced by a simple model of a blackbody and hydrogen nebular emission leaking through a high column density screen of neutral hydrogen in the $n=2$ level ($N_{\rm H,\,n=2}\approx10^{17}\,{\rm cm^{-2}}$), combined with a relatively weak host galaxy, although alternative CE scenarios may also reproduce this reddening. The host galaxy's growing FUV contribution in this model results in a testable UV morphological evolution with wavelength. This work identifies a family of quasi-hostless LRDs that share a common, intrinsically red, rest-UV continuum originating from their central engine.

title: Nearly pristine gas and hard ionizing radiation one billion years after the Big Bang
abstract: The first stars formed out of light elements (H, He, and Li leftover from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis) and began the chemical enrichment of the Universe. Identifying this first-generation population of stars, known as Population III, and understanding their properties is one of the most ambitious goals of modern extragalactic astrophysics. We report the detection of He and H emission lines and extremely low Oxygen abundance in AMORE6, a strongly magnified galaxy at redshift z = 5.725, i.e. approximately one billion years after the Big Bang, with deep James Webb Space Telescope spectroscopy. He II lambda1640 and lambda4686 emission lines are detected at 16.7 sigma and 4.0 sigma significance, respectively. The observed He II-to-Hbeta ratios are consistent with predictions for extreme ionizing radiation fields and the low chemical compositions typical of Population III stars. Oxygen abundance of the interstellar medium is estimated to be 8 x 10^-4 solar from weak [OIII]lambda4363 and lambda5008 lines, consistent with an almost pristine environment, perhaps enriched by the Pop III stars themselves. Although we cannot exclude alternative sources of hard ionizing radiation, such as accreting black holes, these observations offer the first view of the extremely low metallicity environment where the Universe's first stars are predicted to be born. The data show that such pockets of pristine gas still exist one billion years after the Big Bang and that they are dominated by very massive stars.

title: Atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances of young stars with APOGEE -- II. Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, and Sulphur abundances in Orion
abstract: We derived the abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, and iron in young G-, K-, and M-type stars (effective temperatures of 3500--5900 K) using APOGEE-2 infrared spectra. Our final sample comprises 195 slow rotators ($v\sin i$ $\leq$ 30 km~s$^{-1}$) in the Orion complex (Orion A, B, OB1, and $λ$~Ori). The abundances were determined using MARCS model atmospheres, atmospheric parameters derived with \tona, and the \bacc\ code. We obtained median abundances of $ε$(C) = 8.37$\pm$0.10, $ε$(N) = 7.35$\pm$0.16, $ε$(O) = 8.63$\pm$0.08, $ε$(S) = 7.19$\pm$0.18, and $ε$(Fe) = 7.45$\pm$0.05. Nitrogen is subsolar ([N/H] $=-0.48$), whereas carbon, oxygen, sulphur, and iron are within 0.1 dex of the solar values. We find no spatial structure within the Orion subgroups, and the only significant difference is a 0.29 dex lower nitrogen abundance in Orion A than in Orion OB1, which does not extend to the other elements. Compared with 430 nearby main-sequence stars analysed in the same way, Orion shows carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen abundances lower by 0.1--0.2 dex, although consistent within the errors, whereas sulphur and iron differ by less than 0.07 dex. We also compare our abundances with nebular abundances of HII regions and star-forming galaxies: the stellar abundances of oxygen, sulphur, and iron are higher, with the largest offset in iron, although the agreement in abundance ratios improves when temperature inhomogeneities and dust depletion are taken into account.

title: An early interaction between the Sagittarius dwarf and the Milky Way I: Fossil signatures in the phase-space structure of the disc
abstract: Several independent lines of evidence point to an early encounter between the Milky Way and the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy $5$-$7$ Gyr ago. We present four controlled $N$-body+hydro simulations, one of an isolated host galaxy and three of a single interaction between a Milky-Way-like host and a Sagittarius-like satellite on an unbound polar orbit. Relative to the fiducial satellite (with total mass $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$), one run increases the satellite's mass by a factor of $1.5$ and another its crossing speed by a factor of $1.4$, giving pericentric speeds of $466$-$634$ km s$^{-1}$ at pericentric radii of $R\simeq15$-$18$ kpc. Comparing the present-day, phase-space structure in radial bins by age of newly-formed thin-disc stars across the runs, we find that stars that existed at the time of the passage are thickened by up to $\sim37$ per cent in mass-enclosed height and heated by up to $\sim5$ km s$^{-1}$ in vertical velocity dispersion relative to the control, while stars formed after the passage are unaffected. The heating signature is also evident when comparing the age-vertical velocity dispersion relation against a heating relation with a power law of $0.38$, obtained by fitting the isolated host. A single, disc crossing from an early interaction thus suffices to leave lasting, datable fossils in the age-resolved vertical structure of a galactic disc. The fiducial run's dispersion jump of $\sim4$ km s$^{-1}$ matches best with that observed in the outer low-$α$ disc of the Milky Way (Das et al. 2024), corresponding to a perturber mass of $0.7\times10^{11}$ M$_\odot$, with a velocity of $466$ km s$^{-1}$ at a pericentric radius of $16.7$ kpc, though the inversion from jump amplitude to perturber mass is good only to a factor of $\sim1.5$.

title: A TESS Search for Optical Variability in Intermediate-mass Black Hole Candidates
abstract: Optical variability of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) probes accretion onto black holes. We study the optical variability of AGNs in the mass range of intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs, $10^{2-6}\,M_\odot$), whose expected variability damping timescales are of order days. We use the high-cadence photometry of the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) to search for optical variability within its individual 28-day sectors. By applying the Quaver light-curve reduction pipeline and designing artifact-aware variability metrics, we identify 3 sources with high-confidence variability and 17 sources with medium-confidence variability. Fitting damped random walk (DRW) models reveals a tentative timescale-mass correlation in a small, metric-selected subset, but not in the full sample. ZTF difference-image aperture photometry reveals long-term fractional variability of 1.8-7.4% in the high-confidence sources, while most medium-confidence sources have variability below 1%. This study demonstrates that the dense cadence and repeated full-sky observations of TESS are valuable for detecting IMBH optical variability, while also being limited by its instrumental artifacts and relatively shallow field.

title: Hotter than Little Red Dots: Two Quasars with $T\sim10^4\,\mathrm{K}$ blackbody-like continua at $z\sim4$
abstract: Gas envelope models of Little Red Dots (LRDs) predict a transition from cool ($T\sim5000\,\mathrm{K}$), gas-enshrouded accretion to an exposed quasar, but observational candidates remain scarce. We identify two blackbody quasars (BBQs), JADES1180 at $z=3.711$ and GTO1215 at $z=4.552$, among 3,553 sources with archival NIRSpec/PRISM spectra. Both show extremely red rest-frame UV ($β_\mathrm{UV}>2.0$) but blue optical continua ($β_\mathrm{opt}<-0.75$), where $f_λ\proptoλ^β$. Their $Λ$-shaped UV-optical continua peak at $λ\approx3000-4000$ Å and are not reproduced by a quasar template reddened with an SMC-like extinction curve. Under the gas envelope interpretation, UV-to-mid-infrared spectral energy distribution fitting indicates $T_\mathrm{env}\approx7600-10300\,\mathrm{K}$ and $L_\mathrm{env}\simeq(3-15)\times10^{45}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, placing both sources just above the typical LRD ranges in temperature and luminosity. Both BBQs show hot-dust emission with $T_\mathrm{dust}\simeq1400-1550\,\mathrm{K}$ and X-ray emission with $L_\mathrm{2-10\,keV}\simeq(1.3-4.5)\times10^{44}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The gas absorption is $N_\mathrm{H}<1.5\times10^{23}\,\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$, indicating Compton-thin absorption sightlines. Both also exhibit far-infrared and millimeter detections, suggesting an additional cooler dust component, potentially associated with their host galaxies. These properties are consistent with a transitional phase in which a hotter gaseous envelope partially exposes the central engine.

title: Precise Interstellar Extinction Estimates for Nearly Ten Million Stars Based on Multiple Spectroscopic Surveys
abstract: Accurate interstellar extinction estimates are vital for revealing the intrinsic physical properties of stars and the dynamic structure of the Milky Way. Based on multiple optical and near-infrared spectroscopic surveys, including LAMOST, APOGEE, GALAH, GaiaESO, SEGUE, and DESI, we use MLPs and polynomial regressions to calibrate giants and dwarfs separately onto the APOGEE parameter scale, constructing a combined spectroscopic catalog of nearly ten million stars with calibrated stellar atmospheric parameters. This catalog not only provides a robust dataset for our extinction measurements, but also serves as a reference sample for estimating stellar parameters from photometric surveys. Both cross-survey comparisons and external comparisons with high-resolution spectroscopic benchmarks show good agreement in the calibrated parameters. By applying the star-pair method to this extensive sample, we obtain precise extinction estimates. Incorporating distance information, we characterize the spatial distribution of extinction covering over 33,000 square degrees of the sky. Comparisons with existing literature demonstrate that our extinction estimates achieve an exceptional precision of 0.019-0.022 mag. The value-added catalog and open-source Python pipeline for line-of-sight extinction released in this work will provide robust support for future Galactic structure studies and photometric calibrations.

title: Characterisation of B-type stars in four young Galactic open clusters. II. Photometric variability with TESS and identification of pulsating stars
abstract: Pulsations and binarity are important properties of massive stars and influence their structure and evolution. Young open clusters are ideal laboratories to study massive stars, since they are mostly coeval and chemically homogeneous. We analyse 82 B-type stars in the Galactic open clusters $h$ and $χ$ Persei, NGC 457, NGC 581, and NGC 1960, which have ages between 15 and 30 Myr. We extract light curves using both simple aperture photometry and a point-spread-function-based method that minimises contamination from crowded fields in full-frame images from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. We successfully extract light curves for 63 stars. The majority have photometric variability caused by pulsations, showing how pulsations are a common property of young B-type stars in clusters. We classify stars into different pulsator types based on their spectral type and frequency spectrum. The most common pulsator class are beta Cephei stars, with 29 stars in total, and we discover pulsation modes in almost all stars with a spectral type of B2 or earlier. All Be stars show pulsations, which supports the consensus of the ubiquity of pulsations in these stars. Finally, we confirm that the majority of early B-type stars are in binary systems, except for two pulsating Be stars and a star with rotational modulation. This indicates that pulsations do not significantly bias the spectroscopic detection of short-period binaries, except for Be stars where the spectroscopic radial velocity variability threshold should be higher than the typical value of 20 km s$^{-1}$.

title: WISDOM Project -- XXIX. Catalogue of CO observations of nearby galaxies and the CO Tully-Fisher relation
abstract: We present Tully-Fisher relations (TFRs) that use carbon monoxide (CO) as the kinematic tracer and Wide-Field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) $W1$-band and Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS) $K_\text{s}$-band magnitudes as tracers of stellar luminosity. CO data were obtained using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array for the mm-Wave Interferometric Survey of Dark Object Masses (WISDOM) project for a sample of $102$ galaxies located at redshifts $z \lesssim 0.03$, with $81$ detections. The best-fitting reverse $W1$-band and $K_\text{s}$-band CO TFRs are $M_{W1}=(-7.18\pm0.93)\left[\log\left(\frac{W_{50}/\sin i}{\text{km~s}^{-1}}\right)-2.6\right]+(-24.04\pm0.13)$ and $M_{K_\text{s}}=(-5.95\pm0.62)\left[\log\left(\frac{W_{50}/\sin i}{\text{km~s}^{-1}}\right)-2.6\right]+(-24.01\pm0.10)$, respectively, where $W_{50}$ is the velocity width of each integrated CO spectrum at $50\%$ of its maximum, $i$ is the galaxy inclination and $M$ is the galaxy absolute magnitude. Our results are in excellent agreement with those of Tiley et al. (2016b), and together they constitute a robust local benchmark for the CO TFR. We however measure a shallower slope and a smaller zero-point offset compared to the relation of Tully & Pierce (2000). Due to the morphological diversity of our sample, we construct separate late-type and early-type galaxy (ETG) CO TFRs, finding that ETGs are $1.40\pm0.39$~mag fainter at $W1$ band and $0.89\pm0.28$~mag fainter at $K_\text{s}$ band at a given velocity width. We also generate and include a comprehensive catalogue of WISDOM CO data products for use in future molecular gas studies.

title: Blowing star formation away in AGN Hosts (BAH) - VI. Warm Molecular Outflows Driven by the Low-Luminosity AGN in NGC 3884
abstract: We use the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) Medium Resolution Spectrograph (MRS) to investigate the warm molecular and low ionization gas outflows driven by the low-luminosity Active Galactic Nucleus (AGN) in NGC 3884. By decomposing the emission-line profiles into multiple Gaussian components, we detect both ionized and warm molecular outflows, traced by [Ar ii] 6.99 um and H2 0-0 S(5), respectively. The ionized and warm molecular components both extend to similar distances from the nucleus, reaching approximately ~1.2 kpc. In addition to an outflow component, we detect a double narrow emission component in both ionized and molecular lines, clearly observed along the minor axis with similar amplitudes, while their intensity ratio varies systematically along the major axis. Both components exhibit similar line widths and centroid velocity distributions, indicating that they are not associated with outflows, but instead arise from gas in the galaxy disk. We estimate that the outflow injects momentum into the interstellar medium (ISM) at a rate corresponding to ~0.015 percent of the AGN bolometric luminosity, consistent with a radiation-driven origin. Assuming a constant outflow rate, the gas reservoir would be depleted on a timescale of ~26 Myr, potentially suppressing nuclear star formation in the host galaxy.

title: Ultra-diffuse Galaxies in the Kilo-Degree Survey: Globular Cluster Systems in Cluster and Field Environments
abstract: Ultra-diffuse galaxies (UDGs) are extreme low-surface-brightness systems whose formation pathways remain debated. Globular clusters (GCs) can trace their early assembly, but wide-area studies of UDG GC populations remain scarce. We study GC systems of 545 high-quality UDG candidates identified in the Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS) with UDGnet, using a dedicated GC-detection pipeline. We identify 24 UDGs with $N_{\rm GC} \geq 3$ (14 associated with groups or clusters and 10 in the field), and use the globular cluster luminosity function to estimate their distances and physical sizes. At fixed luminosity or stellar mass, group- and cluster-associated UDGs tend to have higher GC counts and specific frequencies than field UDGs, although the distributions overlap substantially. Most systems with $S_N \gtrsim 40$ reside in groups or clusters, while field UDGs generally occupy the lower part of the distribution. Group- and cluster-associated UDGs also more often lie near the upper envelope of the $N_{\rm GC}$--$M_\star$ relation. Empirical GC--halo mass relations consequently imply higher halo masses at fixed stellar mass and lower stellar-to-halo mass ratios, although this environmental trend is mild. These findings are consistent with efficient early GC formation followed by suppressed or prematurely quenched field-star formation, suggesting that GC-rich UDGs may represent an extension of the dwarf-galaxy population. The environmental trends may reflect differences in early assembly, quenching, infall, and survival histories rather than a sharp field--cluster dichotomy.

title: Predicting HCN, HCO$^{+}$, multi-transition CO, and dust emission of star-forming galaxies
abstract: We present an analytical model of a turbulent clumpy star-forming disk that reproduces the spatially resolved observations for 6 molecular lines and 3 continuum bands at 250-700~GHz in the central 30~pc of the Circinus Galaxy. Using the properties of the stellar disk as input, and when matched to the line and continuum emission, the model yields the Toomre $Q$ parameter, mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$, metallicity $Z$, and cosmic ray ionization rate $ζ_{CR}$. These in turn are used to infer the gas properties (surface density, velocity dispersion, and radial velocity) as well as the star formation rate. Our main findings from the model include a low CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor that varies with radius in the range $α_{\rm CO}=0.5$--1.5 $M_{\odot}$pc$^{-2}/({\rm K\,km\,s}^{-1})$, close to the canonical value for such environments. It shows that CO(3-2) is a poor tracer of the gas mass surface density $Σ_{{\rm H}_2}$ on these small scales, which is better represented by molecules such as HCO$^+$(3-2) with higher critical density. The steep relation between $Σ_{{\rm H}_2}$ and star formation rate surface density $\dotΣ_*$ is typical of compact starburst systems, and the star formation rate (10~$M_{\odot}$kpc$^{-2}$yr$^{-1}$ averaged over the disk) is high enough to drive a wind. Despite this, and in contrast to typical large scale galactic disks, the energy injection rate into the ISM is dominated by gas inflow through the disk rather than the supernova rate. As such, the decreasing inflow rate at smaller radii could be caused by a wind, or indicate a recent increase of the mass inflow from larger scales. We suggest that such variations in the inflow rate could be associated with the nested spiral structures which have been observed in Circinus.

title: Revisiting the Double Cluster in Perseus: Are NGC 869 and NGC 884 a true binary system?
abstract: We perform a comprehensive study of the Double Cluster in Perseus, NGC 869 and NGC 884, to investigate their nature and evolutionary state. By combining new CCD $UBV(RI)_{KC}$ photometry with high-precision astrometry and photometry from \textit{Gaia} DR3, we determine robust astrophysical parameters, including colour excess, distance, and age. Our analysis confirms that both clusters are young, with an age of $12\pm1$ Myr, and share similar photometric distances of $2.29$ kpc. By integrating these observational constraints with completeness-corrected mass estimates and a suite of N-body simulations, we examine the kinematic and phase-space properties of the system. We find that the internal kinematics of NGC 884 exhibit a stronger and more coherent expansion signature than NGC 869. Our dynamical simulations demonstrate a rapid increase in the separation of the pair during the first 100 Myr, exceeding $1$ kpc. These results indicate that the system is not currently gravitationally bound and does not constitute a binary cluster. Instead, the Double Cluster is presently unbound, and the forward integrations predict that its components will continue to diverge under the influence of their relative motion and the Galactic potential.

title: Baryon-Enhanced Strong Lensing Signatures of Self-Interacting Dark Matter Subhalos
abstract: Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) is generally expected to suppress subhalo strong lensing through core formation, with subsequent gravothermal collapse potentially enhancing it. We show that compact stars can make a viable population of galaxy-hosting SIDM subhalos more efficient lenses than their cold dark matter (CDM) counterparts. When the baryonic potential weakens or reverses the inner velocity-dispersion gradient, SIDM halos suppress or bypass core formation, allowing inner densities to grow from early times. The evolved SIDM subhalos produce larger deflection angles and tangential caustics than in CDM. Such galaxy-hosting subhalos also dominate the galaxy-galaxy strong-lensing (GGSL) budget in clusters, yet lie far below the resolution of cosmological simulations. We calibrate a baryonic parametric SIDM model to predict their effects in the three most massive TNG300-1 clusters, finding GGSL cross sections 1.4--2.7 times those in CDM, comparable to the excess inferred in recent analyses. Baryon-enhanced SIDM lensing can thus account for the observed GGSL excess and predicts stronger perturbations from luminous satellites, testable through resolved distortions of background arcs and rings.

title: The relation between DCN/DNC ratios and gas temperature in late-stage massive star-forming regions using Yebes observations
abstract: Deuterated molecules probe the physical and chemical evolution of molecular clouds and star-forming regions. Their abundances depend on temperature, density, and evolutionary stage. DCN and DNC are relatively abundant deuterated isomers that probe temperature-dependent deuterium chemistry. Although [HCN]/[HNC] is often thought to increase in warmer gas, the temperature dependence of [DCN]/[DNC] remains less well constrained. To investigate how [DCN]/[DNC] depends on the gas kinetic temperature, we observed the $J$=1-0 transitions of DCN, DNC, H$^{13}$CN, HN$^{13}$C, HC$^{15}$N, and H$^{15}$NC toward 101 late-stage massive star-forming regions using the Yebes 40m telescope. Gas kinetic temperatures were estimated from CH$_3$CCH 5-4, whose rotation temperature is closely related to the kinetic temperature of dense gas. These temperatures were adopted in the column density calculations and in the analysis of temperature-dependent abundance ratios. We find a moderate positive correlation between the abundance ratio [DCN]/[DNC] and kinetic temperature, which is statistically significant and indicates that DCN becomes progressively more abundant relative to DNC in warmer gas. A weak negative correlation with temperature is observed for $D_{\rm frac}({\rm HNC})$, whereas no statistically significant correlation is found for $D_{\rm frac}({\rm HCN})$. The [HCN]/[HNC] ratios show substantial scatter and no statistically significant correlation with temperature, possibly due in part to optical-depth effects in the $^{13}$C isotopologues and the limited sensitivity of the $^{15}$N isotopologue observations. These results suggest that [DCN]/[DNC] may be governed not only by HCN/HNC isomeric chemistry but also by temperature-dependent deuterium fractionation pathways and the chemical evolution of dense gas.

title: Disentangling Disk and Broad-Line Region Continuum Emission in a Sample of Active Galactic Nuclei
abstract: Recent continuum reverberation-mapping measurements of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) indicate that the inter-band time lags are significantly larger than those predicted by the light travel times across the standard thin model. In addition, the observed $u$-band excess suggests the presence of diffuse continuum (DC) radiation originating in the broad-line region (BLR). Spectroscopically, the Balmer and Paschen jumps in DC emission are unique indicators to quantify the contributions of the BLR to the observed continuum. Here, we study the DC contributions of 31 AGNs, whose spectra are obtained with the Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS) on the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and with X-shooter on the Very Large Telescope (VLT). In each spectrum, at least one of the Balmer and Paschen jumps is covered. For each object, we performed radiative transfer calculations using Cloudy within the Locally Optimally-emitting Clouds (LOC) model to construct source-specific DC spectral templates. We quantified the DC contribution by incorporating these templates as continuum components in spectral decomposition. The average ratio of the DC to total (i.e., disk+DC) continua is ~33% just below the Balmer jump (~3625 Å). The Balmer jump provides a stronger constraint on the DC component than the Paschen jump. Simulations based on mock spectra further demonstrate that an unsuitable template can introduce systematic, wavelength-dependent biases to the inferred DC fraction. Our results underscore the importance of employing appropriate DC templates in the spectral decomposition to infer the substantial DC contribution. Upcoming time-resolved spectra will enable more detailed modelling and tighter constraints on the disk and BLR.

title: High-precision proper motions toward the Galactic bulge Baade's window from a decade of DECam observations
abstract: A complete characterization of the Galactic bulge stellar populations could offer important clues on the formation and evolution of our Galaxy. However, most bulge fields are hampered by high stellar crowding, strong interstellar extinction, and by heavy contamination from foreground disk stars. We aim to derive proper motions (PMs) towards the Baade's window by using DECam observations, extending kinematic studies of the Galactic bulge below the turn-off to a much larger field of view. We combined three datasets observed with DECam in the $r$-band spanning a ${\sim}$ 10-year baseline. As a pilot study, we only analyzed the field covered by a single detector. We developed an astrometric calibration pipeline that corrects for the DECam tree-ring pattern and residual distortions, tying all positions to the Gaia DR3 reference frame, and used them to derive PMs. We isolated the bulge population through a strict cut in $μ_{\ell^\ast}$, refined with a Gaia DR3 parallax selection. We measured PMs for $48\,239$ stars in the pilot field, with a median uncertainty of $0.65$ mas yr$^{-1}$ at $r_0<18$ mag. Our PMs agree closely with Gaia DR3, and reaches ${\sim}1.5$ magnitudes deeper than Gaia and a comparable depth to VIRAC2 in terms of relative completeness. We found velocity dispersions along Galactic longitude and latitude of $σ_{μ_{\ell^\ast}}=2.76\pm0.03$ mas yr$^{-1}$ and $σ_{μ_b}=2.49\pm0.02$ mas yr$^{-1}$ for the Galactic bulge, consistent with HST studies. We estimated a foreground contamination of ${\sim}14\%$ before any kinematic selection. The cleaned color-magnitude diagram reaches below the main-sequence turnoff, and shows no evidence for a large population younger than ${\sim}4$-$5$ Gyr in this field. Moreover, since the LSST camera shares the same CCD technology as DECam, this work offers a valuable precursor for crowded-field astrometry in the Rubin era.

title: A High-Resolution Stellar Extinction Map of M31 from PHAT and PHAST Photometry
abstract: High-resolution extinction maps of resolved external galaxies, such as M31, are crucial not only for accurately correcting dust extinction and reddening toward individual sources within the galaxy, but also for characterizing the distribution and evolution of interstellar dust in external galactic environments. We aim to construct a high-resolution and large-coverage stellar-traced extinction map of M31, based on multi-band photometric data from the HST PHAT and PHAST surveys. Using a stellar template library built from the PARSEC stellar evolution models and adopting the average extinction law of M31, we apply a matching method analogous to the SPar algorithm to derive A_V values for approximately 65 million stars. The extinction map is then generated using a HEALPix adaptive-resolution scheme. The resulting map covers approximately two-thirds of the star-forming disk of M31, with a maximum spatial resolution of 1.61 arcsec. The median extinction across the map is A_V = 1.24 mag. Comparison with previously published stellar- and dust-emission-based extinction maps shows broadly similar large-scale morphology, while differences remain in the extinction values. The extinction map further reveals fine-scale features such as inter-arm filaments, supernova-driven cavities, and spur-like structures. The map has been publicly released through the NADC platform and is expected to serve as an important observational basis for extinction correction in subsequent astronomical observations and for related M31 scientific studies.

title: Broad-line ambiguity in IC 1495
abstract: Published analyses disagree on whether the 2004 6dFGS spectrum of IC 1495, a barred Seyfert galaxy in the 2MIG isolated-galaxy catalogue, contains broad H-alpha. We compare it with a 2024 SDSS-V/BOSS spectrum to assess changes in broad-line visibility. In 2024, the [O III] profile favours a blueshifted wing with intrinsic FWHM ~640 km/s, while [S II] and [O I] favour single-component fits. Among six H-alpha+[N II] models with free narrow-line kinematics, the BIC-preferred fit includes broad H-alpha with intrinsic FWHM ~2000 km/s. However, adding broad H-alpha worsens the BIC when H-alpha and [N II] share two narrow kinematic components. Broad H-alpha is not detected in the 2004 spectrum under the adopted criterion. Injection-recovery simulations of a reference broad component (FWHM ~1930 km/s; broad-to-narrow H-alpha flux ratio 0.82) yield recovery fractions of 27-35% in baseline simulations and 11-55% across the grid. At 1.5 times this flux ratio, baseline recovery rises to 42-55%. Aperture and flux-calibration uncertainties limit absolute line-flux comparisons. Narrow-line excitation, Chandra spectroscopy (intrinsic N_H ~2.3 x 10^23 cm^-2 in the fiducial model), and long-term optical and mid-infrared variability support an absorbed, variable Seyfert nucleus. The model-dependent 2024 broad-H-alpha candidate and limited 2004 sensitivity do not establish a change in broad-line visibility between the epochs.

title: The role of gas on the collisional runaway path to supermassive black hole seeds
abstract: The origin of supermassive black holes (SMBHs) remains unclear, despite observational evidence for their rapid formation in the early Universe, as evidenced by active galactic nuclei (AGN) at high redshift. In this paper, we investigate stellar dynamics in dense, gas-embedded clusters. We explore how gas influences the runaway collision process and the subsequent formation of SMBH seeds in a global instability scenario. We perform a series of coupled N-body and SPH simulations using the AMUSE framework, with the stellar and gaseous components interacting gravitationally via the BRIDGE method. We use 12 initial condition models with equal-mass stars following Plummer distributions, with total masses ranging from $10^3$ to $5 \times 10^5~M_{\odot}$, virial radii from $0.005$ to $0.1$ pc, and stellar masses of $1$, $10$ and $50$ $M_{\odot}$. For each model, we perform four simulations with gas fractions ranging from 0\% to 20\%, resulting in a total of 48 simulations. The gas is sampled with the same spatial distribution as the stars, with a mass ratio per particle of $m_{\rm SPH}/m = 0.01$, where $m$ is the stellar mass. We find that in most of our simulations, higher gas fractions lead to the formation of more massive black hole, as the core collapses earlier, triggering collisions through gas--star interactions. Our results show increases in BH mass of $\sim 8\%$ for low gas fractions, to $\sim 44\%$ at 20\% gas fraction. The core collapse time is also shortened, with the strongest reduction at $20\%$ gas fraction ($\sim 27\%$). The transonic regime of our initial conditions is where dynamical friction is most efficient in principle. Although our simulations do not fully resolve this effect, gas--star interactions are the principal mechanism driving the enhancement in BH formation efficiency, in the absence of other dissipation mechanisms.

title: Dynamical friction on an extended satellite revisited
abstract: The original formulation of Chandrasekhar dynamical friction (DF) was developed for a point-like particle moving in a infinite and homogeneous medium. However, despite very useful order of magnitude estimates of the slowing-down time scales of a test mass in more realistic finite-sized models, high resolution $N-$body simulations often hint at a breakdown of Chandrasekhar's formalism (typically overestimating the effect of DF) for massive satellites sinking in the host galaxy. More advanced semi-analytical treatment of the DF expression managed to partially reduce said discrepancy, even though an accurate comparison with numerical simulations still remains difficult, specifically due to the interplay between the DF force and the tidal stress effects on an extended stellar systems sinking in the gravitational potential of the parent galaxy or halo. In this study we perform ad hoc $N-$body simulations of a satellite orbiting in a simple spherical galaxy model, for different values of the initial orbital eccentricity, satellite mass, scale radius and velocity anisotropy profile of the host model. We adopt an $N-$body code where the self-consistent interaction among the particles representing the galaxy can be substituted by the effect of the static smooth potential of the system's continuum limit. Moreover, the satellite itself is either modeled with $N_{\rm sat}$ particles or represented by a single particle with an effective size parametrized in the form of the force exchanged with the other simulation particles representing the galaxy. We find that, at fixed galaxy model and satellite mass, the more extended the satellite, the weaker is the effect of DF. This trend, which is found for both isotropic and radially anisotropic host systems, is particularly evident for orbits with initial orbital eccentricity exceeding $\approx0.3$.

title: Little Red Dots at Cosmic Noon: Spectroscopic Identification and Broad-Line Properties
abstract: We present Keck/NIRES, VLT/X-shooter, and Magellan/FIRE spectroscopic follow-up observations of photometrically selected Little Red Dot (LRD) candidates targeting H$α$ at $2<z<3$. The apparent decline of LRDs at cosmic noon raises the question whether they retain the spectra of the high-redshift population. From a parent sample of 266 unresolved sources with V-shaped broadband SEDs, identified in 19.9\,deg$^2$ of the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program Deep/UltraDeep fields, we observe 24 and confirm broad H$α$ in 6. The remaining 18 candidates show no broad H$α$. Four have Ly$α$ redshifts, which place H$α$ outside our coverage for two. The other 14 have only photometric redshifts, so their H$α$ coverage is uncertain; they may have incorrect photometric redshifts, broad H$α$ fainter than $L_{\mathrm{H}α}\approx3\times10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$, or not be LRDs. All six broad H$α$ lines are best fit by exponential profiles, with FWHM $\approx 950$--$2150$ km s$^{-1}$. Three show Balmer absorption, all show Balmer decrements above Case B ($Hα/Hβ\approx 8$--$34$, though H$β$ is not detected), and four have V-shaped SEDs consistent with JWST-selected LRD samples. Archival \textit{JWST}/NIRCam imaging and NIRSpec spectroscopy independently confirm one source as an LRD. One of the six is X-ray detected at a luminosity typical of ordinary AGN and is better described as a broad-line AGN. Only one of seven dust-reddened F2M quasars and two of 38 heavily reddened quasars at $2<z<3$ meet typical JWST V-shape criteria. Four of the six sources with broad H$α$ ($67$\%) resemble JWST-selected LRDs, showing that ground-based photometric selection and spectroscopy can identify LRDs.

title: Effects of Preionisation in Radiative Shocks IV. A Spectral Grid Library of fully Radiative Shock Models with Time--Dependent Precursor
abstract: Here we present an extensive set of shock models calculated using an improved version of the MAPPINGS shock and photoionization code. The new version of MAPPINGS, namely MAPPINGS V, has a greatly improved treatment of the precursor emission, a more robust adaptive-mesh shock solver (Sutherland & Dopita 2017), and new atomic data compared to MAPPINGS III, which was used by Allen et al. (2008) to create their widely used shock model grid. The new shock model library covers the shock velocity range 50-1000 km/s, and a wide range of initial conditions and updated abundances. We highlight how the newer models compare to the earlier grid, and discuss where the shock models are most likely to approximate conditions for various types of astrophysical objects. The emission that one expects to observe depends on a variety of factors, including the velocity of the shock, the density and abundance of material the shock is encountering, the magnetic field and the effective age of the shock.
